wording: In English validation data (280 measurements, 145 healthy participants, four placebo-controlled psilocybin studies), the four-factor Mystical Experience Questionnaire (MEQ30) and the six-factor MEQ40 showed acceptable to good confirmatory fit, and six of the eight Psychedelic Experience Scale subscales showed high internal consistency.
counterevidence_limits: Drug-context sample; psychometric fit says the questionnaire measures reports consistently, not what the experiences are of.
verification_phrases: K04|280 English PES measurements || K04|acceptable to good model fits

wording: Graziosi et al. (2026) did not reproduce reported effects of experimentally induced awe on agency detection, prosocial behaviour or well-being across online, laboratory and virtual-reality inductions, including three online direct replications with 2.5 times the original sample sizes.
counterevidence_limits: Mostly online (MTurk) samples; induction strength can differ from originals.
verification_phrases: K05|2.5 times the original sample sizes || K05|past findings also were not reproduced

wording: In SIM-SPIRIT-A (illustrative originals of 50 per group, published only if p < .05), published effects averaged d = 0.48 when the true effect was zero; a replication at 2.5x n has power .35 for a true d = 0.2, so three failed replications still have probability .27 (pre-registered H1 of < .10: not supported). A run of failures like K05's argues against medium effects (d = 0.3: .04) more than against small ones.
verification_phrases: n/a (simulation or framework claim; verified against execution records)

wording: Keltner & Monroy (2026) review evidence that awe is a distinct emotion expressed in mouth and gaze activity, vocal bursts and upward head orientation with 'some degree of universality' (in one paradigm, five cultures overlapped in 63% of awe-expression elements) and elaborated culturally in choral music, dance and art of the sublime.
locator: K06 review sections on facial, vocal and cultural expression
counterevidence_limits: Narrative review by proponents of the basic-emotion approach.
verification_phrases: K06|overlapped in 63% of the elements of the awe expression

wording: In SIM-SPIRIT-A, a binary 'all four subscales above a cut' classification was unstable even with subscale reliability .90: only 72% of people classified at test were classified again at retest (kappa .67; pre-registered H1 of at least 80%: not supported). Binary 'complete experience' counts carry more measurement noise than the subscale reliabilities suggest.
counterevidence_limits: Illustrative cut (60th percentile on each subscale), not the published criterion, which was not read.
verification_phrases: n/a (simulation or framework claim; verified against execution records)

counterevidence_limits: Generic; not an audit of any original study.

wording: Transcendence (descriptive): traditions describe mystical experience as contact with or realisation of a reality beyond ordinary experience (S15, which excludes paranormal experiences). Questionnaires such as the MEQ measure how people report such experiences; whether the experienced reality exists is a philosophical and spiritual question the measurements do not settle.

Hypothesis: self-transcendent emotions such as awe are one pathway linking spirituality to well-being (Report 4). After K05's failed replications, this remains a hypothesis without robust experimental support; it would be tested by preregistered, adequately powered induction studies with manipulation checks.
verification_phrases: n/a (simulation or framework claim; verified against execution records)
